cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We aimed to map deviations from normative ranges of whole-brain major WM tracts for individual patients to investigate the similarity and differences among schizophrenia (281 patients subgrouped into the first-episode, subchronic and chronic phases), ASD (175 patients), and ADHD (279 patients). [...] We hypothesized that the WM profiles of deviance and idiosyncrasy in schizophrenia, especially in the earlier phase of the illness, would be similar to ASD and ADHD. However, as schizophrenia progressed from the first episode to the chronic phase (based on the stratification), the level of this similarity among schizophrenia and neurodevelopmental disorders would decrease. We also hypothesized that there would exist different linked dimensions of cognitive function and WM deviation profiles, cutting cross schizophrenia, and neurodevelopmental disorders. [...] normative modeling, combined with stratification based on disease stages of schizophrenia, is needed to better model individual variation in brain alterations and explain the relationships between schizophrenia and neurodevelopmental disorders.
